messages.author: a4fda7a7721880a6
messages.subject: Hide navbarmenu item?
parts:
Hello,

I have a shiny app with a UI build from a navbarPage() with various tabPanel() and navbarMenu() items. I'd like to hide certain navbarMenu() items should certain conditions not be met (i.e. particular input files not being present). Is such a thing possible?

Many thanks,

Jon

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Hide navbarmenu item?
parts:
You can do it, but it involves a bit of JavaScript and a basic knowledge of CSS selectors.  If you're familiar with those on a very basic level or if you're willing to put in a couple hours to learn, then you can see this StackOverflow answer to guide you:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/31703241/activate-tabpanel-from-another-tabpanel/31719425#31719425

That question deals with disabling a tab, but the solution for hiding a tab would be almost identical. It doesn't deal with menu items, but if you understand that solution then you should be able to expand on it to make it work for menu items as well. If you don't know JS or CSS at all, it might take you a bit of time and effort to understand the StackOverflow answer. Hope this helps!

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Hide navbarmenu item?
parts:
Actually, I just realized that hiding should be a lot easier than disabling because it doesn't require any JavaScript, you could just use `shinyjs::hide()` if you know the CSS selector of the menu item.  Ignore my previous answer, here's some code to demonstrate how to hide a tab, this is much simpler and should be fairly easy to use for menus


library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)


shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    useShinyjs(),
    checkboxInput("foo", "Show tab2", TRUE),
    tabsetPanel(
      id = "navbar",
      tabPanel(title = "tab1",
               value = "tab1",
               h1("Tab 1")
      ),
      tabPanel(title = "tab2",
               value = "tab2",
               h1("Tab 2")
      ),
      tabPanel(title = "tab3",
               value = "tab3",
               h1("Tab 3")
      )
    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    observe({
      toggle(condition = input$foo, selector = "#navbar li a[data-value=tab2]")
    })
  }
)

parts:
The solution above did work, though because I wanted to hide a navbarMenu() rather than a tabPanel() (and I couldn't see an obvious way to assign an id or value to a navbarMenu()), I had to resort to nth child (which always tells me I'm doing something unwise):

  observe({
      hide(selector = "#navbar li:nth-child(6)")
  })

(with appropriate conditions of course). So options for conditions added to these elements would definitely be nice, and less hacky.

Jon
